title: They’re made out of weights
summary: An article by Max Leiter exploring the fundamental nature of neural networks, explaining that they are essentially made up of weights - numerical values stored in matrices that transform inputs into outputs through mathematical operations.
problem_solved: Demystifies how neural networks actually work by revealing they are fundamentally collections of weights performing matrix multiplications.
why_valuable: Makes the often opaque internals of neural networks transparent by showing that despite their 'magic' perception, they are just weights and mathematical operations.
